correctness.rationale: The prescribed f(t) is the absorbing first-hitting density for dX=v dt+sqrt(2D)dB, with c=L²/(4D)>0 and b=v²/(4D)≥0. For Q_tau(t)=∫_{max(0,t−tau)}^t f(u)du, Q_prime(t)>0 for t<tau, and for t=tau+s, Q_prime=f(s+tau)−f(s). The log ratio G(s)=c tau/[s(s+tau)]−(3/2)log(1+tau/s)−b tau has G_prime=tau[(3/2)s(s+tau)−c(2s+tau)]/[s²(s+tau)²]. Its quadratic numerator has one positive root and G runs from +infinity to −b tau (or 0 from below if b=0), so a unique descending zero yields the unique strict post-shutoff global maximum. Density unimodality makes delta<m<delta+tau and gives 0<d t_star/d tau<1 and d delta/d b<0 by implicit differentiation. Dimensionless substitution yields w=aT+(3/2)log(1+Tw)+w/(1+Tw) with w=c/delta, T=tau/c, a=bc. Root-order estimates supply all three T→infinity regimes, including varying aT/log T→theta. Independently reconstructed the G derivative symbolically and solved representative regimes: (T,a)=(100,0) gives delta≈0.0958106364483 for c=1, and (100,1) gives delta≈0.00877020045074; both match exact density-equality and slope signs. Source verifier is finite evidence only, not the infinite proof.
residual_risks: Does not cover negative drifts or changed boundary conditions; the normalized first-hitting density assumption is specifically v≥0.
The original verifier is floating point and samples finitely many points, so its tests have no universal coverage.

value.rationale: Finite continuous-rate contaminant or tracer release at an absorbing downstream receiver is a mathematically natural transport observable. Its time of maximum loading after shutoff, strict reaction to source duration and drift, and the singular b=0 versus fixed b>0 delay scales with a quantitative crossover are substantive model-sensitive information not given by the classical impulse mode or by temporal moments. In particular, the driftless delay decays as inverse log T while fixed positive drift yields inverse T, so the limit is genuinely nonuniform as drift approaches zero. The result is an exact self-contained family theorem with clear physical and mathematical motivation, not simply a numerical fit, arbitrary parameter slice or new label on a textbook identity.
residual_risks: Idealized model does not cover sorption/reaction/recirculation or concentration measurement as opposed to first-passage absorbed flux.
Potential classical implicit coverage may reduce mathematical priority although the observable is independently motivated.

limitations: Only one-dimensional homogeneous constant drift/dispersion, L,D,tau>0, v≥0, perfect absorbing first-passage receiver and constant-rate source [0,tau].
Peak times are for absorbed first-arrival mass flux Q_tau, not resident concentrations or finite-capacity receptors.
The driftless, fixed-positive-drift, and varying-drift formulas are as T→infinity and not numerical approximations uniformly at all moderate T.
No conclusion for first-passage distributions under negative drift, time-varying coefficients, sorption, nonabsorbing boundaries or coupled interactions.
